consensus_summary: Sapphire’s settled primary biblical-symbolic meaning is heaven, the pavement/firmament, and the throne-glory or manifest presence of God (Ex 24:10; Ezek 1:26; 10:1; Rev 21:19), with secondary elaborations in purity, heavenly-mindedness, preciousness, and variable tribal/apostolic assignments.
book_summary: Sapphire is the full moon in its enthroned and bridal form—the clear sapphire likeness at God’s throne (tohar/clearness as throne-glory that can cease), a brightness worn not owned, and identified with Issachar.
consensus_core_identification: Heaven / sky-pavement / divine throne-glory and presence
book_core_identification: The full moon in enthroned and bridal form (as the throne’s sapphire likeness)
boundary_disagreement: Consensus (and the book’s own common-view note) treats the referent as the blue of heaven/sky and throne-likeness with no lunar identity; the book replaces that referent with the full moon (bridal/enthroned) and adds Issachar and ‘worn not owned’ conditions.
material_contradiction: The same throne-theophany images cannot have as their primary symbolic identity both ‘the blue of heaven itself / divine throne-glory’ and ‘the full moon’; accepting the lunar bridal identification requires rejecting the consensus primary referent.
rationale: Reduced cores diverge: consensus centers sapphire on heaven/throne-glory; the book centers it on the full moon as that likeness. Shared citations (Ex 24; Ezek; Rev) and the minority Issachar label do not preserve the consensus category—they are re-read to support a different referent the consensus explicitly lacks and the common-view note flags as non-standard. This is replacement of the central identification, not mere narrowing or added detail.
strongest_objection: The plain theophany texts compare the sapphire pavement/throne to the clear body of heaven (sky), not the moon; the lunar-bridal reading is a synthetic chain (tohar–Ps 89 moon/throne–Song bride) rather than the texts’ own identification.
